subject: pugs with allergies
one_liner: A shared workspace for your pug's immune system, so no reaction gets escalated twice.
brand_voice_notes: Enterprise collaboration copy applied to a dog's respiratory system, played completely straight. Everything is a process. Nothing is ever marked resolved. The pugs hold job titles and speak in performance-review register. No cuteness, no winking, no exclamation marks. The product is sincerely proud of features that help nobody.

hero.sub: Dander gives every allergen its own channel, every flare-up its own thread, and your pug an account they will never log into. Twelve households have described it as thorough.

features.title: One channel per allergen
features.blurb: Chicken protein, storage mites, the neighbour's lawn, and whatever happened in the car in March each get their own room. Cross-posting is disabled at the org level, because that is how an outbreak becomes a conversation.

features.title: Flare-ups open as threads
features.blurb: A sneeze starts a thread. The thread stays open until someone marks it resolved. Nobody has ever marked one resolved. After four months the thread stops being an incident and becomes the record.

features.title: Presence, kept honest
features.blurb: Your pug's status syncs from the regional pollen index and updates itself hourly. It has read 'itchy' since April. We have chosen not to intervene.

pricing_tiers.name: Sniff
pricing_tiers.tagline: One pug. One allergen. No history worth keeping.
perks: 90 days of reaction history, then it is gone
A single channel named general, which you cannot rename
Vet integration in read-only, meaning it reads and says nothing

pricing_tiers.name: Pro Snout
pricing_tiers.tagline: For households that have accepted this is ongoing.
perks: Unlimited allergens and unlimited unresolved threads
Escalation to a human who is not a vet but is available
Export the full record as a PDF nobody in the house will open

pricing_tiers.name: Kennel Compliance
pricing_tiers.tagline: For breeders, boarding operations, and one very organised couple in Utrecht.
perks: Single sign-on for everyone with a key to the house
Seven-year retention on every sneeze, per our own policy
A dedicated success manager who owns a cat and has disclosed this

demo_screen_concept: A three-column workspace client for a single pug's immune system. Left rail: workspace switcher reading 'Reginald's House' with a member count of four, then a channel list (#general, #chicken-protein, #storage-mites, #lawn-next-door, #the-car-incident, #vet-escalations) with unread counts, plus direct messages from Histamine Response, Left Ear, and The Vet's Front Desk. Centre: a timestamped message feed per channel, posts from Reginald (the pug), Priya (the owner), and a Pollen Index bot that only posts numbers, with inline thread previews that expand in place, reaction chips using word labels rather than emoji, and a composer that actually posts what you type. Right rail: a flare severity meter for the active channel, an unresolved-thread counter that never reaches zero, and the pug's auto-synced status. Interactions: switch channels, expand and collapse threads, add a reaction, post a message, and a search box that filters the feed live.

images.rationale: Full budget of 4 spent. Hero taken because the inflatable-vinyl direction is material rather than typographic and the hero panel is built to hold a laminated photograph. Demo assets skipped because the demo screen is a chat client: channel rails, message rows and threads, all HTML, nothing photo-shaped. Remaining three went to testimonial headshots, since the testimonials are attributed to pugs with job titles and a deadpan employee-directory portrait is the whole joke.

design_direction.style: Welded inflatable vinyl, pool-deck daylight mode. The page is staged as a set of air-filled vinyl panels welded, valved and laid out on a pale pool deck, as if a collaboration company ordered its entire brand identity from a manufacturer of swimming floats. One light mode only, no dark variant. Explicitly absent, because the previous seven entries used them and this one may not: chenille felt patches, engraved brass plates, prismatic or holographic foil, acrylic slabs, vitreous enamel plaques, terrazzo speckle, galvanized zinc panels, hazard chevrons, rivets, pharmaceutical fold creases, blister wells, leaded came, stained glass, risograph misregistration, halftone dot screens, and knockout ink blocks. Also absent: glassmorphism, backdrop blur, neon, bento lattices, and any gradient placed behind body text. Four motifs carry the entire page. (1) The bladder: every card, tier, quote and nav pill is a single air-filled panel with a 26px corner radius, a soft 22px drop shadow at 14 percent of the ink colour offset 10px down, an inset 2px highlight along the top-left interior in white at 55 percent, and an inset 3px shade along the bottom-right interior in the panel's own hue darkened, so each panel reads as pressurised rather than flat. Nothing on the page has a corner sharper than 12px and nothing is a rectangle. (2) The weld seam: a 2px dashed line in the panel hue at 40 percent, inset 10px from the panel edge and following its full radius, the way a pool toy is heat-sealed a centimetre in from its own perimeter. Every panel has exactly one seam, closed, never partial. (3) The valve: a 20px circle in the accent orange with a 5px inner ring of background colour and a 1px ink hairline, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the pricing tier mark and the section marker, placed half-overlapping the panel's top-left seam corner so it reads as pushed into the surface. Never more than one valve per panel except in lists. (4) The deck: the page ground is flat #DCEBF0 carrying a fixed, non-animated wash of two very wide radial gradients in white at 6 percent, positioned top-left and bottom-right, suggesting wet concrete under overcast light and never reading as texture or noise. Section dividers are a single 3px rounded rule in #B9D3DC with 999px caps, never full-bleed, always inset to the content column. Headings are Bricolage Grotesque at 700 and 800, set sentence case, tight at -0.02em, large and flush left, its slightly irregular widths doing the work that a rounded toy face would otherwise do badly. Body is Instrument Sans at 17px with a 1.62 line-height and a 68-character measure. Every figure that pretends to be telemetry (severity scores, thread counts, timestamps, unread badges, pollen indices, prices) is DM Mono with tabular figures, set in recessed wells one step darker than their panel with the inset shade only and no highlight, so numbers read as pressed into the vinyl rather than printed on it. Colour is rationed the way the pattern brief asks: the page is pool blue and pale deck almost everywhere, and float orange #F2713F appears only on valves, the primary CTA fills, and the single highlighted pricing tier, so the eye lands on conversion points without being told to. Icons are inline SVG at a uniform 1.75px round-capped stroke, never filled, never emoji. Motion is pneumatic: panels inflate in on reveal from scale 0.97 and opacity 0, buttons squish to scale 0.985 with their shadow tightening to 8px on press and restoring on release, valves compress 1px on hover, severity meters fill once on entering the viewport and hold, all on 200ms ease-out and all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.

fonts.body: 'Instrument Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: B2B team-messaging SaaS landing page built on the floating-cards-on-an-unbroken-ground pattern: the deck is continuous and does the branding, panels sit on it at varied offsets, and the one saturated accent is reserved for CTAs. Sections run hero with product photograph, three welded feature panels, three testimonial panels with pug headshots, a three-panel rate table with the middle tier inflated, and a closing handoff panel to the workspace demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Pneumatic. Inflate on reveal (scale 0.97 to 1, 200ms ease-out, 40ms stagger), squish on press (scale 0.985, shadow 22px to 8px), valve compress 1px on hover, severity meter fills once and holds. No parallax, no float loops, no bounce. All gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns above 900px, stacked below. Left: an oversized Bricolage headline flush left, a 68-character subline, the orange CTA as an inflated pill with a valve at its left shoulder, and a DM Mono micro-row reading workspace metadata (MEMBERS / CHANNELS / UNRESOLVED). Right: a 16:9 pug photograph seated inside a vinyl panel with the full bladder treatment, seam and valve included, so the photo arrives as a print laminated into a float rather than as a bare image. A single inset severity strip runs under the photo in DM Mono.
